clue.text: Journey by road that is weaving?

indicators.note: weaving suggests threads crossed and interlaced, so the letters that follow are shuffled together

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A question about a road trip that zigzags across the carriageway.
explanation.definitionFit: A ride is a trip taken in a vehicle or on horseback, a straightforward synonym for a journey.

clue.text: Rise? Look to rise around start of breakfast

indicators.note: around means the word for look encloses the letter taken from breakfast
to rise means the built word is read upwards in this down clue, reversing it

parts.note: a leer is a sly or lecherous look

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of breakfast

explanation.surface: Advice to someone getting up: glance up at the start of the morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: LEER around B gives LEBER, which 'to rise' turns upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebel is to rise up against authority, a verb sense of rise, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Co-ed muddled over university call for paperwork, perhaps

indicators.note: over means the jumbled letters sit above the rest in this down clue
muddled means the letters of co-ed are mixed up

parts.note: to page someone is to call them over a speaker or pager

explanation.surface: A confused co-ed student at university calls about paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muddled' makes DECO from the letters of Co-ed.
explanation.definitionFit: Decoupage is decorating surfaces with cut-out paper, so it is an example of work with paper.

clue.text: In shock, being forced to improvise?

definitions.meaning: someone stunned into silence cannot find any words
a speaker with no prepared address must make things up on the spot

explanation.definitionFit: Speechless means struck dumb by shock, and whimsically also means lacking a prepared talk.

clue.text: Favouring the writer's articles about Greek figure

parts.note: pro means in favour of
the writer refers to the setter, me; the 's is a link
the is the definite article
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Supporting an author's essays on a figure from Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to Prometheus, the Titan who stole fire, so it means concerning that Greek figure.

clue.text: Famous statue recalled from Athens or Ephesus

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A celebrated sculpture remembered from a visit to one of two Greek cities.
explanation.walkthrough: The run SORE hides in 'Athens or Ephesus'; 'recalled' reads it backwards. EROS is the statue above the fountain at Piccadilly Circus in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure of Eros at Piccadilly Circus is one of London's best-known statues.

clue.text: One's apologising for eating it

parts.note: eating it sounds like a meal, but the idiom is to eat this dish when humbly admitting a mistake

explanation.definitionFit: To eat humble pie is an idiom for making an abject apology, so whoever apologises eats it.

clue.text: Racetrack: be unhappy about second tripping up

indicators.note: about means the reversed word for be unhappy goes around the letter for second
tripping up suggests something upended, so the word is read upwards in this down clue

parts.note: to mope is to be gloomy and unhappy

explanation.surface: A racegoer is upset at a horse finishing second after a stumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tripping up' turns MOPE into EPOM, which goes about S.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom is the Surrey racecourse that stages the Derby, an example of a racetrack.

clue.text: Church worker mostly succinct when cornered by the Devil

indicators.note: cornered by means the trimmed word is trapped inside the Devil's name

parts.note: Satan is the Devil

indicators.note: mostly means the word for succinct loses its last letter

parts.note: crisp means brief and to the point

explanation.surface: A terse member of church staff confronted by the Devil.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacristan looks after a church's sacristy and its sacred vessels, so is a church worker.

clue.text: Grass given up, newer drug taken, in casual agreement

indicators.note: taken means the drug letter is taken inside the reversed grass word
given up means the word for grass is read upwards in this down clue

parts.note: hay is dried grass
E stands for ecstasy, a relatively new recreational drug

explanation.surface: Someone quits cannabis but takes a newer drug, with a casual nod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given up' turns HAY into YAH, and E goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeah is an informal way of saying yes, used in casual agreement.

clue.text: Fully expounded letters written by noted graduate

definitions.text: Fully expounded letters written by noted graduate

parts.words: Fully expounded letters written by noted graduate
parts.note: the degree letters after a music graduate's name (BMus) spelt out in full; noted puns on musical notes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' here means working with musical notes, not famous.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of a music degree is what the abbreviation BMus stands for, held by a graduate of notes.

clue.text: Expression of disgust covered by subsequent hilarity

indicators.note: covered by means the disgust word sits inside the word for subsequent

parts.note: subsequent means coming afterwards, later
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: A grimace of revulsion is soon hidden by laughter that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilarity is loud merriment, the sound of people laughing, a close synonym.

clue.text: Former students, almost all Union men, gutted by one

indicators.note: almost means the word all loses its final letter
gutted means the insides of men are removed, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Graduates who are trade union members are let down by a single person.
explanation.definitionFit: Alumni are the graduates or ex-pupils of a school or university, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Fish startles, found on tree, lacking tail

indicators.note: found on means the first piece sits on top of the second in this down clue

parts.note: rocks means shakes or startles

indicators.note: lacking tail means the tree's name loses its last letter

parts.note: the almond is a nut tree

explanation.surface: A fish is alarmed to find itself up an almond tree with no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock salmon is a British fishmonger's name for dogfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock salmon is a trade name for dogfish or similar fish sold in British chip shops.

clue.text: Row about a head of agency being female

indicators.note: about means the word for row goes around the letter A

parts.note: a din is a loud noise or row

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of agency is taken

explanation.surface: A dispute concerning whether an agency's chief is a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana is a woman's name, so it serves as an example of a female, crossword-style.

clue.text: Impetuous type's ridiculous road speed

indicators.note: ridiculous means the letters of road speed are wildly rearranged

explanation.surface: A reckless driver's speed on the road is absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw, a bold and rash person.

clue.text: A very quiet girl's upset over last arrest

indicators.note: over means the earlier pieces sit above the final one in this down clue

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

indicators.note: upset means the word for girl is turned upside down in this down clue

parts.note: her refers to a girl; the 's is a link
the end is the last part

explanation.surface: A shy girl is distressed by an arrest at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To apprehend a suspect is to arrest or seize them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Animal track — clue securing form of proof

indicators.note: securing means the word for clue holds the rearranged letters inside it

parts.note: a hint is a clue

indicators.note: form of says the letters of proof are put into a new shape

explanation.surface: A detective's clue to an animal's trail that provides proof.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoofprint is the mark left by a hoof, one kind of animal track.

clue.text: Complexity that will confuse any critic

indicators.note: confuse means the letters of any critic are muddled together

explanation.surface: Something so intricate that any reviewer would be baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Intricacy is the quality of being complicated or detailed, a synonym for complexity.

clue.text: Stroll out?

parts.note: read as walking while out cold, that is unconscious, rather than going out for a walk

explanation.definitionFit: Walking about while asleep is a stroll taken when you are out for the count, a cryptic reading.

clue.text: Defeated, but not initially swallowed up

indicators.note: not initially means the word for defeated loses its first letter

parts.note: beaten means defeated

explanation.surface: Beaten, but only after being consumed at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been swallowed up has been consumed, a past participle synonym.

clue.text: Puzzle with R in, not T, may call for this

definitions.text: Puzzle with R in, not T, may call for this

parts.words: Puzzle with R in, not T, may call for this
parts.note: a crossword where a solver pencilled in R instead of T needs the mistake rubbed out

explanation.walkthrough: Puzzle reads like a verb but means a crossword with a wrong letter written into it.
explanation.definitionFit: An eraser rubs out a wrongly entered letter, which is what such a puzzle requires.

clue.text: Joint article on painter left unfinished

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: left unfinished means the painter's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Paul Klee was a Swiss-German painter

explanation.surface: An article about an artist who abandoned his work incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the joint between the foot and the leg, an example of a joint.

clue.text: Beauty treatment? Item of manicure rejected, in fact

indicators.note: in means the reversed tool goes inside the word fact

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: rejected suggests something sent back, so the word for the manicure item is turned round

parts.note: a nail file is a manicure tool

explanation.surface: In truth, a manicure tool was turned down during a beauty session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in fact' reads as a mere link meaning actually, but fact is the container and 'rejected' gives the turned-round ELIF.
explanation.definitionFit: A facelift is cosmetic surgery to tighten the skin, an example of beauty treatment, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Worry about Sun's initial position at daybreak?

indicators.note: about means the word for worry goes around the letter from Sun

parts.note: to eat at someone, as in what's eating you, is to worry them

indicators.note: initial means the first letter of Sun is taken

explanation.surface: Concern over where the sun first appears in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun rises in the east, so that compass point is its position at daybreak.

clue.text: Time to show change in current plaything

parts.note: an eddy is a swirl where a current changes direction

explanation.surface: A moment to show how electric current alters.
explanation.definitionFit: A teddy is a teddy bear, a child's soft toy.

clue.text: Girl with style going topless

indicators.note: going topless means the word for style loses its first letter in this down clue

parts.note: class means style or elegance

explanation.surface: A stylish young woman goes bare-chested.
explanation.definitionFit: Lass is a mainly northern British and Scottish word for a girl or young woman.

clue.text: How dressing for dinner may make you anxious?

definitions.text: How dressing for dinner may make you anxious?

parts.words: How dressing for dinner may make you anxious?
parts.note: dressing is the condiment rather than clothes, and anxious means eager, so a keen relish leaves you eager

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing for dinner' suggests putting on formal clothes, but it is a sauce, here the hot condiment, and the idiom means very eager.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means extremely eager, keen in both its senses, from the sharp yellow condiment.

clue.text: Taking extra deliveries? Please tell

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by one bowler
do is used as please, as in do come in
to sing is slang for telling or informing to the police

explanation.surface: A request to hear about getting more parcels than usual.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdosing means taking more of a drug than is safe, taking an excess.

clue.text: Dramatist craftily omitting introduction

indicators.note: omitting introduction means the word for craftily loses its first letter

parts.note: slyly means craftily

explanation.surface: A playwright who cunningly skips the opening of his work.
explanation.definitionFit: John Lyly was an Elizabethan playwright, author of Euphues, so he is an example of a dramatist.
